summary: Restored intel-core-001's snapshot (9c1861e) excluding features/; git diff --stat against the snapshot printed nothing and every restored path is owned. Finding 1: IntelPlayerState.pending is now one PendingSighting | null holding a set of types (PendingSightingType); a carrier-sighting body is { kind, tick, seenTick, sightings: [{ type, reason, sector, name }] } with one entry per type from the same older snapshot. step.ts: capped or data-less free triggers join the set (defer); at each boundary, and when an uncapped free trigger fires, flushPending replans every pending type: journal rumor, no-lead, or together in one sighting message; types without a readable snapshot entry stay pending. The cap is one sighting message per player per snapshot. Existing scripted tests were adapted only to the new body/pending shape (same scenarios and values). New scripted tests (alpha preset on the test sea): two pending types delivered together at the next boundary; a third trigger joins the set and all three go out in one message. The property checker now asserts after every step that each player has at most one pending message with unique types, and that each deferred type is delivered at the first boundary after it was capped, or else the checker proves it ineligible (dropped) or unreadable in the previous snapshot (still pending). EXERCISED adds sighting:deferred-delivered and sighting:several-types. Finding 2: the checker verifies every rumor: a cache target only when no sealed source of that type exists outside the recipient's active journal, and a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. A new scripted test over 24 seeds, where a source and a cache are both eligible, checks that start, targeted and fresh rumors always pick a source. Mutation checks (run by hand, then reverted): delivering only the first pending type fails both new scripted tests and the alpha property run; letting caches compete with sources fails both scripted preference tests and two property runs. docs/intel.md now describes the settled rule. Checks run: npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run test:unit (572 passed), npm run test:integration (36 passed), npm run build (smoke passed), all exit 0. After that, a comment-only rewrap in step.ts; typecheck and the intel unit tests were rerun and pass.
open_assumptions: The per-entry reason in a sighting message records which free trigger (start/fresh/replacement/targeted) asked for that type. The message has no top-level reason, since a merged message can mix triggers.

When an uncapped free trigger fires between boundaries, the pending message is flushed then too, so it goes out together with the new type rather than waiting. Within the same snapshot this can only add data, never an extra message, because the older snapshot does not change.

A pending type whose previous snapshot shows no other carrier stays pending for the following boundary (unchanged from intel-core-001). The checker allows this case and verifies it against the recorded snapshot.
